from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class ExtractionSchema(BaseModel):
    candidate_name: str
    experience_years: int = Field(ge=0)
    skills: list[str]

# Passed to API runtime via response_format schema constraint
json_schema = ExtractionSchema.model_json_schema()

content.tldr: Guaranteed structured outputs in production rely on constrained decoding via Context-Free Grammars (CFGs) or token masking during inference, rather than hoping prompt instructions are obeyed.
content.simple_explanation: Instructing an LLM to 'respond only in JSON' fails intermittently on edge cases because next-token prediction can emit conversational preambles or unescaped quotes. Production-grade systems use grammar-constrained decoding (such as llama.cpp GBNF grammars, Outlines, or OpenAI/Gemini Structured Outputs). At each token step, the engine parses the active state against the JSON schema and masks invalid token logits to negative infinity, making syntactic deviation mathematically impossible.
content.real_world_example: An electronic ticket vending machine with physical buttons: if you are at the step to select train quantity, all alphabet buttons are physically locked out and only number buttons accept presses.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: Relying on post-hoc regex or Pydantic retries adds round-trip latency and operational failure rates. Constrained decoding guarantees 100% schema compliance on the very first generation pass without extra network hops.
